entries.title: Scottburgh Beach Fishing | Shad and Big Blacktail Caught
entries.description:
I spent a beautiful morning at Scottburgh Beach on the KwaZulu Natal South Coast, where a number of anglers were fishing from the rocks.

I did not do much fishing myself, but I took out the camera and captured some of the action. A few shad were caught, along with some seriously impressive blacktail.

Scottburgh Rock is a fantastic place to cast a line, enjoy the ocean and experience the beauty of the KZN coastline.

If you enjoy fishing, outdoor adventures and videos showcasing beautiful places around South Africa, please like this video, share it with your fellow anglers and subscribe to Juelz T for more.

Monster Garrick at Winklespruit | KZN South Coast | 4 MASSIVE Garrick caught | Live bait fishing
entries.description:
Pa and the team headed down to Winklespruit this past week in search of some monster Garrick — and guess what? They found exactly what they were looking for! 

The team managed to land 4 beautiful Garrick, with the biggest weighing an incredible 13kg. We used live Shad as bait and slid them out using braid and line.

It turned out to be an amazing morning of fishing, with plenty of action and some serious fish!

To make it even more special, Pa gave his cameraman Trev the opportunity to fight and land a beautiful Garrick of his own. It was Trev’s first time fighting a fish of this size, and what an experience it was!

Another fantastic day on the water with Pa and the team.

entries.title: Sardine Run 2026 | Port Edward | Up Close With a Sardine Netting
entries.description:
The Sardine Run 2026 continues to surprise us!

Today I was back in Port Edward on the KZN South Coast, where I managed to capture another sardine netting. But this time, there was no drone in the air.

This entire video was filmed from the ground, giving you an up close look at what actually happens during a sardine netting.

By the time I arrived, the net had already been dropped and the team was hard at work pulling it towards the shore. I followed the process from just metres away, capturing the incredible teamwork and physical effort required to bring a net full of sardines onto the beach.

You’ll also see the divers working in the water alongside the net, helping to control it and prevent fish from escaping.

Once the catch reaches the beach, we get right up alongside the net where you can see and even HEAR thousands of sardines shimmering and moving together.

Then the next stage begins as the team starts filling crate after crate with fresh sardines.

Watching a sardine netting from this close gives you a completely different appreciation for just how difficult and physically demanding the process really is.

And considering we’re already late into August, the Sardine Run continues to surprise us. Just when you think it’s over, the sardines show up again!

If you enjoy my Sardine Run coverage and videos showcasing KwaZulu Natal, please LIKE this video, SUBSCRIBE to Juelz Visuelz and turn on notifications so you don’t miss the next adventure.

Let me know in the comments: Have you ever watched a sardine netting this close?

📍 Port Edward, KwaZulu Natal, South Africa

entries.title: Sardine Run 2026 | Glenmore Beach | The Sardines Are BACK!
entries.description:
Just when we thought the Sardine Run 2026 was over… the sardines showed up again! 🐟🌊

After weeks with very little sardine activity along the KZN South Coast, many of us thought this year’s run had finally come to an end.

Then, seemingly out of nowhere, sardines appeared at Glenmore Beach!

I managed to get there in time to capture a single net being pulled, with crowds gathering along the beach to witness another unexpected chapter of the 2026 Sardine Run.

That’s the beauty of the Sardine Run. Just when you think it’s finished, the ocean can surprise you all over again.

entries.title: Unit 6 Arena Park | Chatsworth From Above Ep. 6
entries.description:
Welcome to Episode 6 of Chatsworth From Above.

Today our journey through Chatsworth takes us to Unit 6, better known as Arena Park.

And this may be one of the most visually interesting episodes of the series so far.

From above, we're able to capture Arena Park together with some of the most recognisable landmarks in Chatsworth, including Chatsworth Stadium, the Chatsworth Cricket Oval, Arena Park Swimming Pool, Chatsworth Centre and R.K. Khan Hospital.

But this episode isn't only about what these places look like today.

We go back into the history of Unit 6 and explore how Arena Park developed, the origins of its name, why it developed differently from some of Chatsworth's other units, and how the wider precinct became such an important centre for sport, recreation, shopping and community life.

⚽ We revisit the glory days of Chatsworth Stadium, including its famous association with Manning Rangers and their historic triumph as the inaugural Premier Soccer League champions in the 1996/97 season.

🏏 We explore the Chatsworth Cricket Oval and the area's longstanding connection with cricket.

🏊 We look at Arena Park Swimming Pool and the wider sporting and recreational precinct that served generations of Chatsworth residents.

🛍️ We also take a look at Chatsworth Centre, or simply “the Centre” as generations of locals know it, and its development into one of Chatsworth's major commercial landmarks.

🏥 And we explore the history behind R.K. Khan Hospital, which has served generations of families from Chatsworth and surrounding communities since 1969.

There's also an interesting geographical fact hidden in this episode.

Despite their close proximity to Arena Park, Chatsworth Centre and R.K. Khan Hospital are officially associated with Westcliff in current address records.

How many of you knew that?

We didn't feature either landmark during our Westcliff episode, so with both captured so prominently alongside Unit 6 from above, this was the perfect opportunity to include their stories.

This is what Chatsworth From Above is all about.

Not simply capturing beautiful aerial footage, but documenting the history, landmarks and memories that have shaped generations.

💬 NOW I WANT TO HEAR FROM YOU.

Did you grow up in Arena Park?

Which road did you live on?

Which school did you attend?

Do you remember watching Manning Rangers at Chatsworth Stadium?

What are your memories of the Cricket Oval, Arena Park Swimming Pool or Chatsworth Centre?

And did you always consider Chatsworth Centre and R.K. Khan Hospital part of Westcliff, or did you associate them with the Arena Park precinct?

Share your memories in the comments. Some of the most valuable history of Chatsworth lives in the memories of the people who actually experienced it.

👍 LIKE the video if you enjoyed the episode.

💬 COMMENT with your memories of Unit 6.

📤 SHARE this video with someone from Arena Park or Chatsworth.

🔔 SUBSCRIBE and join us as we continue exploring Chatsworth, one unit at a time.

This is Unit 6.
This is Arena Park.
And this is Chatsworth From Above.

entries.title: In Loving Memory of Stephen Tharmiha (Alan Mark) | 1954 – 2026
entries.description:
In Loving Memory of Stephen Tharmiha, affectionately known as Alan Mark

14 January 1954 – 12 August 2026

This video is a celebration of the life, memories and legacy of my dad, Stephen Tharmiha, known to many as Alan Mark.

From photographs of his younger years, his wedding and family life, to birthdays, special moments with family and friends, and videos of him doing what he loved most, playing music and entertaining, this is a journey through a life that meant so much to so many people.

Music was a huge part of my dad’s life. He was a gifted musician and entertainer who performed with bands including The Magnets and Gold Medallions before later performing as a solo artist and one man band. Put a guitar in his hands and the quiet, reserved man many of us knew could suddenly become the life of the party.

But for me, one of the most precious parts of his story came during the latter years of his life.

After suffering a stroke, my dad reconnected with Jesus Christ.

It became one of the greatest privileges of my life to share the love of Jesus with my dad, to speak to him about the Gospel, to pray with him and to serve him communion daily as he reconnected with the Lord and accepted Jesus Christ as the Lord and Saviour of his life.

Included in this video is something I will treasure for the rest of my life: the last prayer I heard my dad pray aloud.

This memorial was originally created and played at his funeral as we gathered to remember and celebrate his life. I am sharing it here so that our family and friends will always have somewhere to return to whenever we want to see his face, hear his voice, hear his music and remember the moments we shared with him.

Dad, your journey on this earth may have ended, but the memories you gave us remain.

The photographs remain.
The stories remain.
Your music remains.
And most importantly, our hope is in Jesus Christ.

"For whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.”
Romans 10:13 NKJV

Rest well, Dad.

Stephen Tharmiha
Alan Mark
14 January 1954 – 12 August 2026

The music lives on. ❤️
